# The index.xml format

This page is for developers who publish packages, run a mirror or debug the Site package step. It describes the
`index.xml` file of a release folder: its elements and attributes, which of them the code reads, and what happens
when one is wrong. The reference implementation is `eZStepSiteTypes::retrieveRemotePackagesList()` in
`kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_site_types.php`.

## An example

Two entries of the 6.0.15 index, the first a required package, the second a site package (one line each in the
file, wrapped here):

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<packages vendor="7x">

<!-- DEPENDENCY PACKAGE LIST -->
  <package name="sevenx_classes" type="contentclass"
           url="https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/sevenx_classes.ezpkg"/>

  <package name="sevenx_multisite" version="6.0-15-stable" type="site"
           summary="7x MultiSite Default Installation"
           description="7x MultiSite Default Installation is a web based CMS solution based on Exponential. ..."
           url="https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/sevenx_multisite.ezpkg"
           thumbnail_url="https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/thumbnails/sevenx_multisite.png"/>
</packages>
```

The whole file: <https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/index.xml> (44 entries).

## The root element

| Element | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<packages>` | yes | The root. The setup wizard refuses any other root with the debug error "Malformed index file." |
| `vendor` attribute | no | `7x` on the server. It documents the vendor; neither the setup wizard nor ezupdate reads it |

Comments and white space between the entries are allowed; everything that is not a `<package>` element is skipped.

## The package element

| Attribute | Used on | Read by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | every entry | wizard, ezupdate | The package name, the same as `<name>` in its `package.xml`. Entries are keyed by name: a second entry with the same name replaces the first |
| `type` | every entry | wizard, ezupdate | The package type. The wizard lists only `type="site"`; the other entries serve to find the URLs of required packages |
| `url` | every entry | wizard, ezupdate | The full address of the `.ezpkg` file. It may point anywhere, not only to the same folder |
| `version` | site packages | wizard, ezupdate | Shown as "(ver. *version*)" and compared with an imported copy. The same text as `eZPackage::getVersion()` of the package (`<number>-<release>` of its `package.xml`), so an imported copy compares equal ([The index version and the package version](what-is-on-the-package-server.md#the-index-version-and-the-package-version)) |
| `summary` | site packages | wizard, ezupdate | The heading of the entry in the Site package step, and its image title |
| `description` | site packages | wizard | The text under the heading |
| `thumbnail_url` | site packages | wizard | The image shown for a site package that is not imported yet; without it a default image is shown |

> **Warning**
> The Site package step writes `description` into the page as it is, not escaped
> (`design/standard/templates/setup/init/site_types.tpl`), and puts `thumbnail_url` into an image address. Keep
> both plain text and plain URLs, and point an installation only at index files you trust.

## How the setup wizard reads it

1. The index address is `RemotePackagesIndexURL` plus `/index.xml` (a trailing slash is not doubled).
2. The file is downloaded like a package, with retries ([When the package server cannot be reached](when-the-package-server-cannot-be-reached.md)),
   into `<cache>/packages/index.xml`, and deleted after it is parsed.
3. If the download fails, the wizard copies `index.xml` from the system repository,
   `var/storage/packages/7x/index.xml`, when there is one ([Offline installs and mirrors](offline-installs-and-mirrors.md)).
4. The file is parsed with `DOMDocument`. A file that does not parse logs "Unable to open index file." and the list
   stays empty.
5. Each `<package>` element becomes an array of all its attributes, so attributes the code does not know are kept
   but ignored.
6. For the list on the screen only site packages are used; for the dependencies of a chosen package the whole list is
   used, looked up by `name`. A required package that is neither imported nor in the index stops the step with
   "Download of package '*name*' failed. You may upload the package manually."

The radio button of a remote entry carries `name|url`. The step treats the choice as a download only when the name
consists of letters, digits and `_` (`/^(\w+)\|(.+)$/` in `processPostData()`); package names follow that rule
anyway ([package.xml required fields](../requirements/package-xml-required-fields.md)).

## How ezupdate reads it

The ezupdate extension's **Package servers** page reads the same format from every server it knows
(`extension/ezupdate/classes/ezupdatepackageservers.php`):

- the index must be at most 1 MiB, and is parsed without network access (`LIBXML_NONET`);
- a root other than `<packages>` gives "The server did not answer with a package index.";
- a `name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,63}$`, other entries are skipped;
- it shows `name`, `type`, `summary` and `version`, next to the version of an imported copy;
- **fetch** accepts only a `url` that starts with `https://`, and a package of at most 256 MiB.

See [Package servers in ezupdate](../admin-gui/package-servers-in-ezupdate.md).

## A minimal index of your own

For a server with one site package that requires one other package:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<packages vendor="example">
  <package name="example_classes" type="contentclass"
           url="https://packages.example.com/6.0/6.0.15/example_classes.ezpkg"/>
  <package name="example_site" version="1.0-0" type="site"
           summary="Example site"
           description="The starter site of Example Inc."
           url="https://packages.example.com/6.0/6.0.15/example_site.ezpkg"
           thumbnail_url="https://packages.example.com/6.0/6.0.15/thumbnails/example_site.png"/>
</packages>
```

Every package that a site package names in `<dependencies><requires>` must either have an entry here or already be
imported on the installation. See [Running your own package server](../your-own/running-your-own-package-server.md)
and [Declaring dependencies](../requirements/declaring-dependencies.md).

## Checking an index

```bash
# well formed?
xmllint --noout index.xml

# every url answers 200?
grep -o 'url="[^"]*"' index.xml | cut -d'"' -f2 | while read -r u; do
  printf '%s %s\n' "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$u")" "$u"
done
```

The second command checks both `url` and `thumbnail_url`. Run both before you publish an index, and before you open
a pull request for the shared server ([Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md)).
